Point Description: Start at the car park on the Penrhys plateau, right by the imagined stage finish.
A site of pilgrimage since medieval times, with a modern statue marking the original shrine.
The high point of the walk, with sweeping views down both the Rhondda Fawr and Rhondda Fach valleys.
The route dips through a stretch of young woodland before turning back towards the start.
A gentle descent back towards the plateau, with Tylorstown and Ferndale visible below.
Loop complete, back at the car park.
Enter the Cwm Clydach National Nature Reserve, close to the route near Llwynypia.
One of the largest surviving ancient oak woodlands in the Rhondda valleys.
A footbridge crosses the brook that gives the reserve its name.
A quiet spot to watch woodland birds, including regular sightings of woodpeckers.
An open meadow section rich in wildflowers through the summer months.
Loop complete, back at the entrance.
Begin at the head of the Rhondda Fawr, where the imagined stage route also climbs.
A steady climb onto open moorland, with the valley falling away behind you.
The high point of the ridge, right at the mountain pass the stage route crosses between the two valleys (~550m).
An exposed descent with wide views down the Rhondda Fach towards Maerdy and Ferndale.
Finish at Maerdy, at the head of the Rhondda Fach.
Start at the car park by Llyn Fawr, a short detour above Treherbert near Rhigos.
Views along the dam wall across the reservoir to the mountains beyond.
A quiet stretch of shoreline path, popular with anglers and birdwatchers.
Open views towards the Rhigos mountain road and the Brecon Beacons beyond.
The path curves back along the eastern shore towards the car park.
Loop complete, back at the car park.
Start at the former Lewis Merthyr Colliery site at Trehafod, near the stage start at Pontypridd.
The preserved pithead winding gear, a landmark of the Rhondda's mining heritage.
Home to the colliery's original ventilation fan house, now part of the museum.
A level, family-friendly stretch alongside the Rhondda river.
Loop complete, back at the entrance.
Start above Maerdy at the head of the Rhondda Fach, close to where the route crosses the mountain pass.
A clearing in the forestry plantation with views back down the valley.
The walk follows the route of a disused mountain tramroad for a short stretch.
A small stepping-stone crossing over a mountain stream.
Loop complete, back at the car park.
